note: On profile he is the closest thing in this batch to the ICP as stated, and he still refused — which makes the two misses the interesting part. Successful holds: Director of Sales for a medtech company at 30, working remotely, senior enough to count as 'something along those lines'. Good-to-great holds emphatically — he opened by saying the intake questionnaire's premise did not apply to him, 'looking for guys trying to lose 10% body fat. Like, I don't have 10% body fat to lose.' Not-deconditioned holds absolutely: 5'10", 160lb, 12-13% body fat, training five days a week. Income is scored a miss on the same basis as the Badrane Hriouch assessment — the constraint is willingness at this price, not capacity, and he ran the numbers explicitly: 'ROI for ROI on this for 6k would just be out of my range' and '4K in the market right now could be 5-6K in the same amount of three months.' Neglected_health is a clear miss and it inverts the criterion: health is the single most invested area of his life — five sessions a week for over a year, daily macro tracking, creatine, a monthly massage membership, a completed chiro and physio programme. The stated ICP describes someone whose health slipped while their career succeeded; Julian's health never slipped, which is precisely why he could not justify the price. He said so himself: 'if I was in like dire straits and needed like some serious assistance... then absolutely, I could see the money being worth it.' The offer as priced reads to the genuinely good-to-great buyer as built for rescue, which is the opposite of what the ICP claims.
